name: relation_paged_oram_q10_matched_temi
status: completed matched-protocol localhost A/B/C correctness benchmark
scope_warning: Ten distinct queries over a controlled 10-entity, 16-edge fixture. All three MP-SPDZ Temi parties ran on one host and timings include protocol preprocessing. This establishes executable composition and comparative overhead on the fixture; it is not evidence of MetaQA runtime, WAN latency, malicious security, or production scalability.

matched_conditions.protocol: MP-SPDZ Temi: semi-honest dishonest-majority, up to two of three passively corrupted servers
matched_conditions.host: three local parties on one machine; non-collusion is not instantiated by this benchmark

results.trace: fixed full scans of the public relation directory/page layout
one recursive ORAM lookup per fixed scheduled KG lookup; uniformly random opened path label, with repeat hiding via a secret stash

results.backend: relation-paged dual recursive read-only ORAM v2
results.trace: one directory ORAM plus a fixed number of page ORAM accesses per scheduled KG lookup; secret descriptors and dummy page zero hide occupancy

metaqa_public_shape_capacity.status: capacity plan followed by one completed Temi execution
metaqa_public_shape_capacity.warning: One successful query is feasibility evidence, not a dataset evaluation. Path-entry counts are not MPC byte or latency predictions. The fresh epoch input remains linear and the dual layout performs two recursive accesses per logical KG lookup.

optimization_and_security_notes: The generated ORAM circuits scan only prior public stash slots and write directly to the current public slot. This removes no secret-dependent operation or trace event.
MP-SPDZ compilation preserves memory order because later repeated-address reads depend on earlier stash writes.
The recursive builder and planner stop before a pointless one-record position-map ORAM, retaining the remaining secret labels in the fixed scanned base.
The current replay-hiding stash remains quadratic in accesses per epoch; database access is sublinear but large query batches are not yet scalable.
All result fields are freshly reshared and reconstructed only by combining the three private output logs.

metaqa_chi_optimization.status: completed matched Temi A/B on the same MetaQA query
metaqa_chi_optimization.unchanged_security: Both runs use statistical_security_bits=80, three Temi parties, fresh independently randomized 3-of-3 shares, fixed access schedules, and client-only reconstruction.
metaqa_chi_optimization.selection: chi=32 is the measured localhost/communication profile. chi=256 remains preferable when minimizing rounds and likely WAN latency. Neither should be made universal without LAN/WAN measurements.

conclusion: On the ten-query fixture, linear relation paging is the practical winner and wide-record ORAM is the faster of the two ORAM variants. The dual relation-paged ORAM now executes exactly at MetaQA storage scale; chi=32 improves its one-query localhost result to 222.463 seconds and 4.229 GB, but this is still not practical and its 35% round increase is likely harmful on WAN. It must be presented as a feasibility backend, not the selected scalable backend.
